answer.rationale: The line is at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer and the contract lapses in 14 days, so a primary-vendor switch (the only option that meets the 18% mandate by itself) is exactly the kind of move that maximizes delivery risk at the worst moment. memory_c4 and memory_c6 support using the low-cost vendor's quote as a market benchmark to renegotiate with the incumbent: that recovered real margin before and preserves the stable integration (memory_c1) rather than introducing a migration during a no-buffer period. memory_c3 argues for a second source eventually, but with capacity for only one decision, de-risking the renewal via negotiation is the higher-value move this cycle; dual-sourcing can follow at the next review. I want memory_c2 verified because it is the sole evidence that the low-cost vendor switch was clean (fast onboarding, accurate invoicing); if that record has caveats (different component, later quality/delivery issues, or savings that eroded), it materially changes whether the quote should be treated as credible leverage or a credible destination. Negotiating terms minimizes TCO pressure without adding delivery risk now, while keeping the verified low-cost option as a live fallback if the incumbent cannot move.
